gaps.criterion_why: The leaf promises venom that worsens 'until treated or thrown off', so the treated case needs a stated expected result.
gaps.observed: The action now tends one colonist and leaves one untended, but the expect reads "its severity rising over the hours; X over the same hours; once immunity completes the severity falls". The 'X' is unfilled, so no result is stated for the tended colonist and nothing compares the two.

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json sc_flamefang_venom: replace 'X' with the tended-versus-untended severity expectation that the def's tending ships

gaps.what: sc_flamefang_venom's expect has a literal placeholder where the tended colonist's result should be, so the 'until treated' half has no expected outcome.
gaps.would_pass: The expect states a checkable comparison for the tended colonist, e.g. 'the tended colonist's RM_FlamefangVenom severity rises more slowly than (or falls below) the untended colonist's at every hourly read from the tend onwards', and a script can evaluate it from the hourly severity reads.

gaps.criterion_why: The contract requires the positive case to show evidence it used the mechanism and a control that rules out the plausible alternative, here 'no colonist was ever exposed'.
gaps.observed: parts_covered_by says "two weeks of ordinary play beside the front is where a colonist would burn or starve, and the walk reads it". The expect only says "no colonist takes a burn standing in fire and none starves at fire duty", and the controls (an early reload and the toggle's on day) say nothing about fire sense. Nothing reads RM_PyreStepAwayFromFire or RM_PyreEatBeforeFireDuty firing at all.

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json: add a staged-exposure step and its switch-off control to sc_walk, or a new sc_fire_sense; point record.json inv_burn_line_fire_clock parts_covered_by at it; file the script part under RIMMANDRAKE_BUILD_PYRELANDS_GAP_SCENE_PARTS_TEN_SCENES_OWED

gaps.what: Fire sense and eat-before-fire-duty are 'covered' by sc_walk only as an absence (nobody burned, nobody starved). The walk never shows a colonist in the fire's path or urgently hungry at fire duty, and has no control, so a colony that never came near the front passes.
gaps.where: scenes.json sc_walk expect/control; record.json inv_burn_line_fire_clock parts_covered_by
gaps.would_pass: A scene (in the walk or its own) asserts the exposure and reads the mechanism: a colonist standing on a cell the front is about to reach takes RM_PyreStepAwayFromFire and leaves it before Fire attaches, and an urgently hungry undrafted colonist given fire duty eats first. Its control, with the PyrelandsFireSense switch off or on a vanilla map, shows the colonist staying put and catching fire (or going to the fire hungry).

gaps.criterion_why: Wet roots is a built temperature effect, so the scene claimed to cover it must run where the effect can show and read the factor it changes.
gaps.observed: record.json inv_ash_field parts_covered_by claims "a crop growing at the biome's heat at all is the cooler-roots read". The sc_ash_watered start asserts only terrain and the wet read, and its expect is about fertility ("about 140% watered and about 70% dry"). The control expects the switch-off strip to grow "at the dry strip's rate", which is only consistent if the dry strip grows at all. In the built source (PyrelandsWetRoots.cs:76-77) wet roots only acts when the cell temperature is above the plant's maxOptimalGrowthTemperature.

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json sc_ash_watered: add the temperature assertion to start and the GrowthRateFactor_Temperature read to action and expect

gaps.what: Wet roots (a crop on watered ash grows as if cooler, dry ash keeps vanilla's heat) is said to be read by sc_ash_watered, but that scene neither asserts nor reads temperature. If the cell is within the crop's growing range, wet roots does nothing and the scene still passes.
gaps.where: scenes.json sc_ash_watered start/expect; record.json inv_ash_field parts_covered_by
gaps.would_pass: sc_ash_watered's start asserts that the cell temperature is above the crop's maxOptimalGrowthTemperature, and each day it reads Plant.GrowthRateFactor_Temperature on both strips. Expect: the watered strip's factor is above the dry strip's, and the dry strip's equals vanilla's for that temperature.

gaps.criterion_why: An immunity claim is only shown when the immune body is demonstrably exposed. The scene's own rules_out already admits this.
gaps.observed: rules_out lists "A's fire never reaching A passing for the heat immunity". The control is a muffalo whose bed the test lights itself, which shows fire burns animals but not that A was ever exposed. The built patch (Patch_FurnaceBeastHeatImmunity.cs, cited in record.json inv_furnacebeast) blocks Fire attaching (CanEverAttachFire) and absorbs heat-armour damage, so exposure has to be read to tell immunity from no contact.

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json sc_furnace_bed: add 'fire on A's cell while A occupies it (asserted per poll)' to action and expect

gaps.what: The furnace-beast's heat immunity is judged by 'A takes no burn injury from its own bed fire', but nothing asserts that the fire reached A's cell while A lay there. A fire that burns out at the patch edge, or a beast that wakes and walks off, passes. The rules_out names this case, but no control rules it out.
gaps.would_pass: The poll reads show a Fire on A's own cell (or heat damage dealt to A and absorbed) for at least one poll while A is on it, and A gains no Burn hediff. The muffalo, in fire on its own cell for the same span, gains a Burn hediff.

gaps.criterion_why: A count threshold that a natural roll can meet does not show the top-up mechanism. The contract asks for a control that rules out the alternative.
gaps.observed: parts_covered_by assigns "the fire-cast top-up (sc_populations' hawk and ashwallow counts)". The expect says "at least two fire-hawks and eight ashwallows", and the control only seeds donors and toggles the allowlist.

smallest_fix.what: scenes.json sc_populations: add the before/after genstep count read, or a genstep-off same-seed control

gaps.what: The fire-cast top-up (GenStep_PyrelandsFireCast: a pair of fire-hawks and eight ashwallows) is read only as 'at least two fire-hawks and eight ashwallows', with no control. A map whose ordinary wild-animal roll already reached those counts passes without the genstep doing anything.
gaps.where: scenes.json sc_populations expect/control; record.json inv_animal_roster parts_covered_by
gaps.would_pass: sc_populations reads the hawk and ashwallow counts after the vanilla animal genstep and again after GenStep_PyrelandsFireCast (or from the genstep's own added-count), and expects the top-up to fill exactly the shortfall to 2 and 8. A control with the genstep disabled on the same seed shows the pre-top-up counts.
